category_overview: All four tools sit on the post-sale side of the customer lifecycle but on different layers. Zendesk AI and Fin compete head-on for autonomous ticket resolution and agent-assist in the contact centre: both now bill per outcome or resolution rather than per seat, and both can run on rival help desks (Forethought AI Agents by Zendesk on Salesforce or Freshworks; Fin on Zendesk, Salesforce, HubSpot or Freshdesk). Gainsight works upstream in customer success, mining the same emails, meetings and tickets for renewal risk and expansion signals, while Qualtrics spans the whole journey, measuring experience and increasingly acting on it through Experience Agents. The 2026 consolidation wave reshapes vendor choice: Salesforce closed its ~$3.6B purchase of Fin in September 2026, Zendesk bought Forethought in March 2026, and Qualtrics absorbed Press Ganey Forsta for $6.75B in May 2026, so CRM and help-desk allegiance now determines which AI is practical to standardise on. Enterprises typically standardise on one help-desk AI (Zendesk or Fin/Intercom) for support, Gainsight or CRM-native tooling for success, and Qualtrics for voice-of-customer, then connect signals through CRM integrations or MCP rather than buying one vendor for everything.

tools.name: Gainsight AI
tools.vendor: Gainsight, Inc. Sold as Staircase AI (the Insight Agent inside Gainsight CS), Atlas (AI-native services) and the Agentic Stack (Agent Studio, MCP, CLI); 'Gainsight AI' is a handbook label, not a product name.
tools.what_it_is: AI layer of the Gainsight CS customer-success platform. Staircase AI reads emails, meetings, tickets, chats and Slack to score sentiment, churn risk, stakeholder disengagement and expansion; Atlas pairs AI renewal agents with human Renewal Agent Managers to run long-tail renewals as a service. It lives in the Gainsight CS web app, Slack, Salesforce and any MCP-compatible assistant.
key_capabilities: Churn-risk, sentiment and stakeholder-disengagement alerts from every customer conversation (Staircase Risk, Expansion and Handoff Analysts)
Health scorecards, playbooks, Customer 360 and renewal/expansion forecasting in Gainsight CS
Atlas managed renewals with humans in the loop, contracted on results
Agent Studio (beta, Claude-powered) to turn repetitive CS workflows into reusable agent skills
Gainsight MCP and CLI expose live customer data to Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot or coding agents
Community Moderation Agent and Skilljar AI Tutor for digital customer hubs
tools.enterprise_data_handling: Stated platform-wide (no tier distinctions published): customer data is 'NOT used to train any LLMs' by Gainsight or its vendors (IBM watsonx, Azure OpenAI, OpenAI; vendor abuse-monitoring retention disabled); every AI feature is off by default until an admin enables it; data is never used outside the tenant. SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, HIPAA, GDPR and Data Privacy Framework; Staircase AI adds ISO 42001, automatic PII anonymization and EU data-centre options. SSO/SAML and RBAC. No FedRAMP; residency options for Gainsight CS beyond the EU Staircase option are not stated.
tools.licensing_pricing: No published list prices: Gainsight CS Essentials (10 full users, 100 customers per user) and Enterprise (20 full users, 200 per user) are 'Request Pricing', with unlimited viewer licences. Announced Oct 2026: from 2027 seat pricing is replaced by value-based pricing tied to ARR and customers managed, with Staircase AI and MCP access included at no extra charge; Atlas is sold on results-based service contracts. Not bundled with any office suite.
tools.integrations: Salesforce (CRM sync, expansion signals, Agentforce MCP beta, Sept 2026 Agentforce and Slack integrations), Slack agent and alerts, mailbox/calendar/meeting, ticket and chat ingestion, Zoom, Gong, HubSpot, MCP clients (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot), Skilljar and Communities.
tools.recent_developments: May 2025: Atlas launched at Pulse as an agent family (Staircase, Renewal, Adoption, Moderation, Slack agent); Staircase AI gained ISO 27001/42001; Skilljar acquired. May 2026: Atlas repositioned as an AI-native services business; 'Agentic Stack' launched with Agent Studio, MCP (175,000+ tool calls), CLI and pre-built agents; Salesforce partnership. Oct 2026: Atlas manages $75M+ customer ARR across 7,000+ agentic interactions; Agent Studio in beta; value-based pricing announced; Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader for the third year. Note the naming shift: Staircase AI appears inside Gainsight CS as 'Insight Agent'.
tools.best_fit_departments: 36 Customer Success (Advanced): direct fit for customer health, renewal-risk detection and success plans; the only department listed, and the right one.
tools.training_notes: Health-score design, reading Staircase risk signals without over-reacting, playbooks/CTAs, human review of agent-drafted renewal outreach, consent and privacy for mailbox and meeting ingestion, deliberately enabling AI features, basic MCP and Agent Studio use. Advanced band, 12-16 hours.
tools.caveats: No public pricing and the model changes in 2027; Atlas is an outsourced service, not just software; mailbox and meeting ingestion needs privacy and works-council review; risk and sentiment scores are probabilistic; Agent Studio is beta; CS data residency beyond EU Staircase hosting is undocumented.

tools.name: Zendesk AI
tools.vendor: Zendesk, Inc. Sold as Zendesk AI on the Zendesk Resolution Platform: AI agents (including Forethought AI Agents by Zendesk), Copilot, Knowledge, QA and Voice.
tools.what_it_is: The AI layer of the Zendesk Suite help desk. Autonomous AI agents resolve customer and employee requests across messaging, email and voice, while Copilot assists human agents and admins inside the Zendesk agent workspace. It is configured in Admin Center; since the Forethought acquisition the agents can also run on non-Zendesk platforms.
key_capabilities: AI agents that resolve multi-step workflows across channels, execute actions in business systems and improve through the Resolution Learning Loop
Copilot: context-aware reply suggestions and autonomous actions for agents, plus service-gap insight for admins
Unified knowledge graph grounding answers in trusted content, with intelligent triage
AI quality assurance scoring 100% of interactions with coaching recommendations
No-code Agent Builder (early access) for custom agents aligned to company policy
tools.enterprise_data_handling: All plans: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001/27018/27701/27017, ISO 42001, CSA STAR AI, FedRAMP LI-SaaS, PCI-DSS; HIPAA BAA requires the Advanced Compliance add-on. Data locality (US, AU, JP, EEA) via the Data Centre Location add-on; some acquired services (WFM, QA, Ultimate) run on GCP in the US, Germany and Belgium. SAML/JWT SSO, 2FA, RBAC, IP allowlists; a Service Data Deletion Policy governs retention. AI data use: Zendesk trains generic cross-account, non-generative classification models on Service Data by default (no PII fields or attachments); OpenAI-powered generative features run under zero data retention and OpenAI never trains on Service Data; every AI feature can be disabled in Admin Centre.
tools.licensing_pricing: USD, annual billing (monthly in brackets): Support Team $19/agent/mo ($25), Suite Team $55 ($69), Suite Professional $115 ($149), Suite Enterprise contact sales; also EUR, GBP, BRL. Included automated resolutions: 5/agent/mo (Team plans), 10 (Professional), custom (Enterprise); additional resolutions $1.50 committed or $2.00 pay-as-you-go. Add-ons (annual): Copilot $50/agent/mo, Workforce Engagement $50, Contact Center $83. Not bundled with any office suite.
tools.integrations: Native Zendesk channels (messaging, email, voice, help centre); action execution into business systems via the Resolution Platform; Forethought AI Agents deployable on Salesforce, Freshworks and other help desks; employee service for IT and HR.
tools.recent_developments: Mar 2026: acquired Forethought (self-improving agents, browser-based automation without APIs, usable without the Zendesk platform). May 19, 2026 Relate: 'Autonomous Service Workforce', omnichannel agents across messaging/email/voice, Agent Builder, outcome pricing on verified resolutions (dual AI verification), platform trained on ~20B interactions, expansion into employee service. ISO 42001 and CSA STAR AI attained. 'Automated resolution' remains the billing unit on the pricing page.
tools.best_fit_departments: 37 Customer Support & Contact Center (Core): direct fit for ticket classification, knowledge search and agent-assist; the only department listed.
tools.training_notes: Agents: Copilot use, verifying AI drafts, escalation handling, PII awareness (Core 6-8 hours). Admins: knowledge hygiene as the AI's source, intent/triage configuration, Agent Builder, resolution-cost monitoring, QA calibration, disabling unwanted AI features (Advanced 12-16 hours).
tools.caveats: Per-resolution billing rises as automation improves; resolution definitions and verification are still evolving; HIPAA and data locality are paid add-ons; generic classification models train on Service Data unless disabled; limited model choice; Agent Builder is early access; FedRAMP only at LI-SaaS level.

tools.name: Intercom Fin
tools.vendor: Fin (the company formerly Intercom, Inc., renamed May 12, 2026), acquired by Salesforce on Sept 10, 2026 and operating within Salesforce AI Labs. Product family: Fin customer agent platform (Fin AI Agent, Procedures, Operator, Fin Voice, Copilot) and the Intercom 2 help desk. The brief's 'Intercom' guess is outdated.
tools.what_it_is: An autonomous AI customer agent that resolves support conversations end-to-end over chat, email, WhatsApp, SMS, voice and Slack. It runs natively inside the Intercom help desk or standalone on Zendesk, Salesforce, HubSpot and Freshdesk, powered by Fin's proprietary Apex models; Fin reports a 76% average resolution rate.
key_capabilities: Autonomous resolutions grounded in help-centre and knowledge content
Procedures: multi-step workflows that take actions in back-end systems
Operator back-office agent and Fin Voice on the low-latency Apex Flash 2.0 model
Built-in testing suites, observability and AI-recommended improvements
Copilot for human agents in the inbox; Fin for Sales lead qualification
tools.enterprise_data_handling: Stated for all Fin customers (no tiering published): SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, ISO 27701, ISO 42001, AIUC-1, HIPAA, GDPR/CCPA. Hosting in the US, EU or Australia. SSO (Okta, Azure AD, OneLogin), SCIM, 2FA, IP restrictions. Training: 'Fin can use anonymized customer data for model fine-tuning, and you can opt out at any time, with data deleted within 30 days' — anonymized fine-tuning is on unless you opt out; third-party model providers are contractually barred from training and hold zero retention.
tools.licensing_pricing: Fin: USD $0.99 per outcome (resolution, procedure handoff, disqualification, self-serve routing) and $9.99 per sales qualification; Fin Voice custom-priced; standalone use on other help desks requires a 50-outcome monthly minimum with no platform fee; 14-day trial. Intercom help desk seats, annual: Essential $19/seat/mo ($29 monthly), Advanced $85, Expert $132; Copilot add-on $29/agent/mo; Pro $100/mo. Not bundled with any suite; Salesforce packaging not yet announced.
tools.integrations: Intercom 2 help desk natively; Zendesk, Salesforce Service Cloud, HubSpot and Freshdesk as a standalone agent; WhatsApp, SMS, email, voice and Slack channels; positioned alongside Salesforce Agentforce post-acquisition.
tools.recent_developments: May 12, 2026: company renamed Intercom to Fin; the help desk keeps the Intercom name and was relaunched as Intercom 2 (rename flagged). June 15, 2026: Salesforce agreed to acquire Fin for ~$3.6B; closed Sept 10, 2026 with Fin continuing independently inside Salesforce AI Labs. Apex Flash 2.0 voice model and outcome-based pricing introduced; pricing unchanged as of Sept 24, 2026.
tools.best_fit_departments: 37 Customer Support & Contact Center (Core): strong fit for deflection, agent-assist and ticket handling; the only department listed.
tools.training_notes: Knowledge-source curation, writing Procedures with guardrails, pre-launch testing against real transcripts, handoff rules, reading outcome reports and 'assumed resolution' rates, Copilot use, deciding on the fine-tuning opt-out. Core 6-10 hours for agents, 12-16 for Fin administrators.
tools.caveats: Assumed resolutions (customer silent for 24 hours) are billable, so costs track volume; ownership change may alter roadmap and packaging; anonymized fine-tuning is default-on; Fin for Sales outcomes only on Intercom deployments; voice is custom-priced; third-party guides cite a $49/mo standalone base while the official page shows a 50-outcome minimum.

tools.name: Qualtrics AI
tools.vendor: Qualtrics (Qualtrics International). Marketed as Experience Agents plus the XM platform's AI features (Qualtrics Assist, Insights Explorer, Conversational Feedback, Edge Audiences); 'XM Data & AI' is the platform announced for 2027. 'Qualtrics AI' is a handbook label, not a product name.
tools.what_it_is: AI inside the Qualtrics XM experience-management suite. Experience Agents detect friction and act in the moment — resolving complaints inside surveys, suggesting and executing approved actions on support tickets, intercepting frustration on websites — while text analytics and Insights Explorer summarise open-ended feedback. It lives in the Qualtrics web platform, embedded surveys and customer digital properties.
key_capabilities: Survey, Digital, Ticket and Frontline Experience Agents operating within policy guardrails and approved compensation limits
Insights Explorer: themes and summaries from open-text voice-of-customer data
Conversational Feedback for adaptive surveys and Edge Audiences synthetic research panels
Reputation Experience aggregating Google, Yelp and Facebook reviews; X-Loop lifecycle diagnostic
Dashboards honouring role-based access and sensitive-data policies
tools.enterprise_data_handling: Platform-wide statements (no tiers published): Qualtrics 'doesn't use your raw customer data to train its AI models' but does build anonymized, aggregated training datasets; sub-processors are contractually barred from training and hold zero data retention; data stays within Qualtrics datacentre boundaries. SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, ISO 42001 (Aug 2025), HITRUST, FedRAMP High and IL4. SSO/MFA, RBAC, TLS 1.2+, AES-256. AWS regions in the US, Europe (Frankfurt, London), Asia Pacific and Japan. Survey agents are incompatible with sensitive-data policies; ticket-agent actions require human approval.
tools.licensing_pricing: No published prices: CX is priced per 'interaction', EX per employee, research per response and video minute — all 'Request Pricing'. Experience Agents are metered per 'Agent Engagement' (an agent's first autonomous action) with 500 free engagements per month for testing, and are limited to the new simplified packaging or Preview Program plus Qualtrics implementation services. Not bundled with any office suite.
tools.integrations: Embedded surveys and websites, support ticketing within the XM platform, review sites (Google, Yelp, Facebook), LangChain LangGraph agent framework, customer-selectable LLMs (self-hosted Llama models by default), AWS hosting.
tools.recent_developments: Mar 2025: Experience Agents unveiled at X4 (built on LangGraph). Aug 2025: ISO 42001. Oct 2025: Experience Agents in production plus Insights Explorer, Edge Audiences and Conversational Feedback. May 2026: $6.75B Press Ganey Forsta acquisition closed. Sept 9, 2026: XM Data & AI platform (simulate, predict, trusted outcomes) announced for 2027 release; X-Loop Diagnostic and Reputation Experience available now.
tools.best_fit_departments: 38 Customer Experience & Service Design (Advanced): direct fit for voice-of-customer synthesis, journey diagnostics and closed-loop service actions; the only department listed.
tools.training_notes: Survey design, validating text-analytics topics, verifying Insights Explorer summaries against source responses, designing agent guardrails and approval workflows, compensation limits, sensitive-data policies, methodological caveats of synthetic audiences, dashboard RBAC. Advanced band, 12-20 hours.
tools.caveats: No public pricing; Experience Agents are gated to new packaging and paid implementation; product terms state outputs 'may be inaccurate or contain material errors' and place verification on the customer; anonymized customer data trains Qualtrics models unless contracted otherwise; XM Data & AI does not ship until 2027; synthetic panels need scrutiny.
